To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) network anonymization is difficult because the structure of the network is used to infer the identities of individuals, 2) the effectiveness of anonymization techniques varies based on network structure, and 3) the effectiveness of network anonymization techniques can be improved by modeling the network structure.

the privacy of networked data is highly dependent on network structure, that there exist network anonymization techniques which are effective in protecting networked data, and that there is a trade-off between privacy and the accuracy of statistical queries.
We quantify privacy risks associated with the release of networked data and show that they vary greatly with network size and structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of protecting the privacy of individuals whose data are stored in networked data structures.
the problem of protecting the privacy of individuals whose social networks are made public.
the problem of protecting the privacy of individuals whose relationships are revealed by networked data sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is the most efficient way of preserving anonymity in social networks.
the paper provides a new method for network anonymization, which has the potential for preserving privacy while still allowing the analysis of networks.
this paper presents a novel approach for anonymizing networks that models aggregate network structures and then allows samples from that model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we quantify the risk of re-identification in social networks and propose a novel anonymization algorithm that preserves network structure while protecting individual privacy.
we have developed a new privacy model and a new anonymization algorithm for network data.

we provide a new approach to anonymizing social networks that is based on the structural properties of the networks and is able to provide a trade-off between the privacy of individual entities and the ability to estimate aggregate network properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of structural re-identification attacks is not constant across networks.

network structure is an important factor to consider when evaluating privacy risks and that network data can be anonymized in a privacy-preserving way that preserves the ability to estimate network properties.
privacy risks in networks are not uniform, but depend strongly on network structure and the type of data that is released.
